Distinguishing from atrial fibrillation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 74-year-old with new palpitations has an irregularly irregular rhythm. No reproducible P waves are seen, and irregularity does not track respiration. A trainee calls this respiratory sinus arrhythmia because the pulse is irregular. Which finding most strongly contradicts that label?

  1. Presence of a palpable pulse
  2. An average heart rate of 88/min
  3. Absence of consistent sinus P waves
  4. Variation in R-R intervals
  5. A narrow QRS complex
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Absence of consistent sinus P waves

Respiratory sinus arrhythmia remains a sinus rhythm; loss of organized P waves suggests another rhythm such as atrial fibrillation.

Understanding the options

Absence of consistent sinus P waves
Respiratory sinus arrhythmia remains a sinus rhythm; loss of organized P waves suggests another rhythm such as atrial fibrillation.
Variation in R-R intervals
R-R variability can occur in respiratory sinus arrhythmia.
A narrow QRS complex
Narrow QRS complexes are compatible with either rhythm.
Presence of a palpable pulse
A pulse does not distinguish these rhythms.
An average heart rate of 88/min
The average rate alone does not determine the rhythm origin.
